en.h1: Side-job income: a clean record that keeps private spending out
en.lead: Separating a side job from private money rarely fails for lack of discipline. It fails because both run through the same account. What needs separating is the record, not necessarily the account.
en.answer: Keep one ledger that holds only the side job: every payment with date, who paid and how, and every expense only if it would not exist without the job. Everything else stays out. What you eventually have to declare is set by your local rules; this page is about the recording method.
paras: The usual pattern: the client transfers to the personal account, materials go on the personal card, the trip there is paid in cash. Three months later nobody can tell which entries belonged to the side job. The shared account is not the problem. The problem is that there is no separate ledger where side-job entries land the same day.

What belongs in it: for each payment, the date, the amount, who paid and by what route (transfer, cash, payment service). For expenses, one question only: would this exist without the side job? If not, it goes in, with the receipt number in the note. Things that are both, like the phone or the internet, get a tag called Mixed and are not split on the spot. How much of them counts toward the job depends on the applicable rules and your situation; sort that out once a month against the official guidance or with an adviser, not entry by entry.

In MoneyTag each side job is its own project with its own ledger: income minus expenses is its net, and private spending never enters. Every entry has a note for client, payment route and receipt number, plus tags such as Materials, Travel or Mixed; the Tags screen totals the same tag across all projects. For handing over, export as CSV or PDF. Data stays in on-device storage. Free to start; unlimited projects, tags and reports are a one-time purchase.

loc.h1: Despesas por projeto: o jeito de descobrir qual cliente deu lucro e qual deu prejuízo
loc.lead: O Pix entra, o cartão sai, tudo na mesma conta. No fim do mês sobra pouco e ninguém sabe dizer qual projeto comeu o dinheiro.
loc.answer: Abra um livro só para cada projeto, lance nele toda receita que cair e toda despesa que só existiu por causa dele, com três etiquetas fixas: material, terceiros e deslocamento. No fechamento, receita menos despesa é o lucro real daquele cliente, e esse número vai para o próximo orçamento.
paras: O erro mais comum do freela é olhar o valor que o cliente pagou e chamar isso de ganho. Só que, para entregar, você pagou um colega para dividir o trabalho, comprou material ou licença de imagem, foi e voltou de Uber para reunião e visita. Somando tudo, sobrou bem menos da metade. Quando conta pessoal e projeto ficam no mesmo lugar, você enxerga o que recebeu, não o que lucrou, e orçamento se faz com o que lucrou.

O método tem dois movimentos: um livro por projeto e três etiquetas fixas. Material é tudo que acaba quando o projeto acaba: impressão, insumo, licença, assinatura usada só ali. Terceiros é o que você pagou para alguém fazer parte do trabalho. Deslocamento é reunião, visita, envio. Não crie uma quarta etiqueta, porque lista longa é o motivo de ninguém etiquetar direito. No fechamento, olhe primeiro o líquido e depois quanto cada etiqueta comeu da receita; no próximo orçamento parecido, some essas três fatias antes de colocar a sua margem.

O MoneyTag funciona exatamente assim: cada projeto é um livro próprio, e receita menos despesa é o resultado líquido daquele projeto. Qualquer lançamento recebe etiqueta, e a tela de Etiquetas soma a mesma etiqueta em todos os projetos de uma vez, então o tipo de custo que vive comendo a sua margem aparece na hora. Cliente de fora pagando em dólar não atrapalha: cada projeto mantém uma moeda-base e o lançamento é convertido com taxa automática ou manual. en.title: Track expenses per project to know if a client paid off
en.meta: Billing is not earning. One ledger per project and three fixed tags show at closing whether a client paid off. MoneyTag is free to start, one-time purchase.
en.h1: Expenses per project: how to tell which client made money and which lost it
en.lead: Payments come in, the card goes out, all in one account. At month end little is left and nobody can say which project ate the money.
en.answer: Open a ledger for each project, record in it every payment that lands and every expense that exists only because of it, with three fixed tags: materials, subcontractor, travel. At closing, income minus expenses is that client's real profit, and that number goes into the next quote.
paras: The commonest freelance mistake is reading what the client paid and calling it earnings. To deliver, you paid a colleague to take part of the work, bought materials or an image licence, and took rides to meetings and site visits. Add it up and well under half remains. When personal spending and project money share one place, you see what you received, not what you earned, and quotes are built on what you earned.

The method is two moves: one ledger per project, and three fixed tags. Materials is anything that ends when the project ends: printing, supplies, licences, a subscription used only there. Subcontractor is what you paid someone else to do part of the work. Travel is meetings, visits, shipping. Do not add a fourth tag, because a long list is why nobody tags properly. At closing, read the net first, then how much of the income each tag took; on the next similar quote, add those three shares in before your margin.

MoneyTag works exactly this way: every project is its own ledger, and income minus expenses is that project's net. Any entry takes a tag, and the Tags screen totals the same tag across all projects at once, so the cost type that keeps eating your margin shows up immediately. A foreign client paying in another currency is no problem: each project keeps one base currency and the entry is converted with a live or manual rate. Free to start; unlimited projects, tags and reports in a one-time purchase.

Record income only when the money lands, with the date; deposit and final balance as separate entries. A quote is not income.
Record each expense the same day and tag it materials, subcontractor or travel. No fourth tag.
On delivery day, read the ledger's net, then check on the Tags screen how much of this project's income each of the three tags took.
On the next similar quote, add those three historical shares first and only then the margin you want. That is your floor.

Yes. One entry each, with dates, so midway through you know what has landed and what is still due, without confusing a quote with money earned.

loc.h1: Как вести рукописные конспекты на iPad, чтобы потом их находить
loc.lead: Сложность конспекта от руки не в том, чтобы его написать, а в том, что через месяц его невозможно найти. Решает это не приложение, а четыре договорённости с самим собой до начала семестра.
loc.answer: Одна тетрадь на курс, печатный заголовок с номером недели и темой на каждой странице, четыре постоянных цвета и PDF лекции, импортированный в ту же тетрадь, — при такой структуре любой рукописный конспект находится за десять секунд.
paras: Начните со структуры до первой лекции. На каждый курс — своя тетрадь или папка, внутри — страницы по неделям. Сверху каждой страницы печатными буквами пишите код курса, номер недели и тему: «Матан, нед. 3, пределы». Печатный заголовок распознаётся надёжнее беглого почерка, поэтому поиск по нему работает даже в самом неразборчивом конспекте.

Цвета нужны не для красоты, а как единая маркировка для всех предметов. Четырёх хватает: тёмно-синий — основной текст, красный — определения и то, что точно спросят, жёлтый — свои мысли и вопросы, оранжевый — связи с другими темами. Если в каждом предмете цвета значат разное, через месяц вы перестанете им доверять. Слайды лекций импортируйте как PDF в ту же тетрадь и пишите рядом с ними то, что преподаватель говорит вслух, а не то, что уже напечатано.

en.title: Handwritten iPad lecture notes you can actually find later
en.meta: Handwritten notes get lost without a system: a notebook per course, four fixed colours, lecture PDF alongside. 100 Notes Studio: free to start, one-time unlock.
en.h1: How to structure handwritten lecture notes on iPad so you find them again
en.lead: Writing the notes is the easy part. The hard part is finding one page of them a month later. That is fixed by four rules you set before term starts, not by the app.
en.answer: One notebook per course, a printed heading with week number and topic on every page, four colours that always mean the same thing, and the lecture PDF imported into the same notebook — with that structure any handwritten page turns up in ten seconds.
paras: Set the structure before the first lecture. Each course gets its own notebook or folder, with pages grouped by week. At the top of every page, print the course code, week number and topic in block capitals: "Calc, wk 3, limits". Block capitals are recognised far more reliably than cursive, so search on the heading works even when the body of the page is a scrawl.

Colours are a filing code, not decoration, and the code has to be identical across every subject. Four is enough: dark blue for the main notes, red for definitions and anything likely to be examined, yellow for your own thoughts and questions, orange for links to other topics. If colours mean different things in different courses you will stop trusting them within a month. Import the lecture slides as a PDF into the same notebook and write beside them only what the lecturer says out loud, never what is already printed.

All of this depends on an app whose search can read your handwriting. In 100 Notes Studio, handwriting recognition runs on the device, and search covers titles, body text, handwriting and attachments without a network connection. Lecture PDFs import into the notebook and take highlights, underlines and handwritten notes, and an audio recording stays attached to the page where you started it. Nested folders, tags and an auto-numbered table of contents hold a whole semester in one structure.

loc.title: Notas a mano en iPad con el método Cornell
loc.meta: Los apuntes a mano se repasan si la página está pensada para ello: preguntas, notas, resumen y PDF juntos. 100 Notes Studio: gratis para empezar, un solo pago.
loc.h1: Tomar notas a mano en iPad: un método de apuntes que luego sí se repasan
loc.lead: Casi nadie vuelve a leer sus apuntes porque la página se escribió para copiar, no para repasar. El método Cornell arregla eso antes de escribir la primera línea.
loc.answer: Divide cada página en tres zonas antes de la clase: una columna izquierda estrecha para preguntas, el bloque principal para notas y cinco líneas abajo para el resumen. Repasar consiste en tapar la derecha y responder a la izquierda; con el PDF de la clase en el mismo cuaderno no hace falta cambiar de app.
paras: El método Cornell no es una plantilla, es un reparto de la página: la columna izquierda ocupa más o menos un tercio del ancho y se deja vacía durante la clase; el bloque derecho recoge lo que explica el profesor; las cinco líneas finales se rellenan ese mismo día con un resumen de dos frases. En un cuaderno digital puedes trazar esas líneas con la regla una vez y duplicar la página, o simplemente marcar la columna con una línea vertical al empezar cada hoja.

Lo que de verdad hace que se repase viene después de clase: antes de 24 horas vuelves a la página, escribes en la columna izquierda la pregunta que responde cada bloque de notas y resumes abajo. Al repasar, tapas la derecha y contestas en voz alta. Si el profesor cuelga el PDF de los apuntes, impórtalo en el mismo cuaderno y escribe al lado sólo lo que dice y no está en las diapositivas; subrayar lo que ya está impreso no es tomar notas.

Para que el método funcione en el iPad, la app tiene que dejar escribir sobre el PDF y buscar luego en tu propia letra. 100 Notes Studio importa documentos PDF y permite resaltar, subrayar y añadir escritura a mano en la misma página; el reconocimiento de escritura funciona en el dispositivo y la búsqueda cubre títulos, contenido, trazos y adjuntos. Las preguntas de la columna izquierda pueden pasar a fichas enlazadas y repetirse con repetición espaciada FSRS, y el audio de la clase queda unido a la página donde empezaste a grabar.

en.title: Cornell notes by hand on iPad: a method you will revise from
en.meta: Handwritten class notes get revised when the page is built for it: question column, notes, summary, PDF together. 100 Notes Studio: free to start, one-time buy.
en.h1: Taking notes by hand on iPad: a class-notes method that gets revised
en.lead: Most notes are never read again because the page was written for copying, not for revising. The Cornell method fixes that before the first line goes down.
en.answer: Split every page into three zones before class: a narrow left column for questions, the main block for notes and five lines at the bottom for a summary. Revising means covering the right side and answering the left; with the class PDF in the same notebook there is no app to switch to.
paras: Cornell is not a template, it is a division of the page: the left column takes roughly a third of the width and stays empty during class; the right block holds what the lecturer explains; the last five lines are filled the same day with a two-sentence summary. In a digital notebook you draw those lines once with the ruler and reuse the page, or just mark the column with one vertical line as you start each sheet.

What actually makes revision happen comes after class: within 24 hours you return to the page, write in the left column the question each block of notes answers, and summarise at the bottom. To revise, cover the right side and answer out loud. If the lecturer posts the notes as a PDF, import it into the same notebook and write beside it only what was said and is not on the slides; underlining what is already printed is not note-taking.

For the method to work on iPad, the app has to let you write over the PDF and later search your own handwriting. 100 Notes Studio imports PDFs and lets you highlight, underline and add handwriting on the same page; handwriting recognition runs on the device and search covers titles, body text, strokes and attachments. The questions from the left column can become linked flashcards reviewed with FSRS spaced repetition, and class audio stays attached to the page where you started recording.

loc.meta: โน้ตลายมืออ่านทวนไม่ไหว มักเพราะไม่ได้แบ่งหน้า: หัวเรื่องบนสุด คอลัมน์ซ้ายไว้ถาม ใช้ 3 สี สไลด์ PDF อยู่เล่มเดียวกัน 100 Notes Studio เริ่มใช้ฟรี ซื้อครั้งเดียว
loc.h1: จดโน้ตด้วยลายมือบน iPad ให้อ่านทวนง่าย: แบ่งหน้า ใช้สี และใส่ PDF สไลด์
loc.lead: ปัญหาของโน้ตลายมือไม่ใช่ลายมือไม่สวย แต่คือตอนใกล้สอบเปิดมาแล้วไม่รู้จะเริ่มอ่านตรงไหน การแบ่งหน้าก่อนเขียนแก้เรื่องนี้ได้มากกว่าการเปลี่ยนปากกา
loc.answer: ก่อนจดให้แบ่งหน้าเป็น 3 ส่วน: หัวเรื่องและวันที่บนสุด คอลัมน์ซ้ายแคบ ๆ ไว้เขียนคำถาม ส่วนขวาไว้จดเนื้อหา ใช้สีแค่ 3 สีโดยให้แต่ละสีมีความหมายเดียวทุกวิชา แล้วนำเข้าสไลด์ PDF มาไว้ในสมุดเล่มเดียวกับโน้ต การอ่านทวนจะกลายเป็นการไล่ดูทีละหน้าที่จบได้ใน 10 นาที
paras: เริ่มจากแบ่งหน้า ทุกหน้าควรมีหัวเรื่องเขียนตัวบรรจงไว้บนสุดเสมอ เช่น ชื่อวิชา สัปดาห์ที่ และหัวข้อ เพราะตัวบรรจงค้นหาเจอง่ายกว่าลายมือหวัด ถัดมาลากเส้นแนวตั้งให้คอลัมน์ซ้ายกว้างประมาณหนึ่งในสามของหน้า ตอนเรียนปล่อยว่างไว้ จดเนื้อหาเฉพาะฝั่งขวา และเว้นล่างสุดไว้ 4-5 บรรทัดสำหรับสรุป เมื่อทุกหน้ามีโครงเดียวกัน ตอนอ่านทวนสายตาจะรู้ทันทีว่าต้องมองตรงไหน

สีมีไว้บอกประเภทข้อมูล ไม่ใช่ไว้ตกแต่ง ใช้ 3 สีพอ: สีหลักสำหรับเนื้อหา สีแดงสำหรับนิยามและสิ่งที่มักออกสอบ สีที่สามสำหรับคำถามหรือความคิดของตัวเอง และต้องใช้ความหมายเดียวกันทุกวิชา ถ้าเปลี่ยนความหมายไปมาจะเลิกเชื่อสีภายในเดือนเดียว ส่วนสไลด์ของอาจารย์ให้นำเข้าเป็น PDF ไว้ในสมุดเล่มเดียวกับโน้ต แล้วเขียนข้าง ๆ เฉพาะสิ่งที่อาจารย์พูดแต่ไม่มีบนสไลด์ การไฮไลต์สิ่งที่พิมพ์มาแล้วไม่ใช่การจดโน้ต

วิธีนี้จะได้ผลเมื่อแอปค้นหาลายมือของเราเจอ 100 Notes Studio รู้จำลายมือและค้นหาได้ภายในเครื่องโดยไม่ต้องต่อเน็ต ค้นได้ทั้งชื่อเรื่อง ข้อความ ลายมือ และไฟล์แนบ นำเข้า PDF สไลด์มาไฮไลต์ ขีดเส้นใต้ และเขียนด้วยลายมือทับได้ในหน้าเดียวกัน คำถามในคอลัมน์ซ้ายเอาไปทำเป็นแฟลชการ์ดและการ์ดเติมคำแล้วทบทวนด้วยตารางเว้นระยะ FSRS ได้ ส่วนเสียงที่อัดในคาบจะผูกกับหน้าที่เริ่มอัด เปิดกลับมาก็ได้ฟังพร้อมโน้ตหน้านั้น

en.title: Handwritten iPad notes that are easy to reread before exams
en.meta: Handwritten notes fail at revision when the page was never divided: heading, question column, 3 colours, slides alongside. 100 Notes Studio: free, one-time buy.
en.h1: Handwritten notes on iPad that are easy to reread: page layout, colours and slide PDFs
en.lead: The problem with handwritten notes is not ugly handwriting. It is opening them the week before an exam and not knowing where to start. Dividing the page before you write fixes that more than any pen does.
en.answer: Divide the page into three zones before writing: heading and date at the top, a narrow left column for questions, the right side for content. Use only three colours, each meaning one thing in every subject, and import the slide PDF into the same notebook as the notes. Revision then becomes a page-by-page pass that takes ten minutes.
paras: Start with the page layout. Every page gets a heading printed in block capitals at the top, such as subject, week and topic, because block capitals are found by search far more reliably than cursive. Then draw a vertical line so the left column is about a third of the page; leave it empty during class, write content only on the right, and keep four or five lines at the bottom for a summary. When every page shares one layout, your eyes know where to look the moment you open it to revise.

Colours signal the type of information, not decoration. Three are enough: a main colour for content, red for definitions and likely exam material, a third for your own questions and thoughts. The meanings must stay the same in every subject; change them around and you stop trusting the colours within a month. Import the lecturer's slides as a PDF into the same notebook as your notes, then write beside them only what was said and is not on the slide. Highlighting what is already printed is not note-taking.

This only works when the app can find your handwriting. 100 Notes Studio recognises handwriting and searches on the device without a connection, across titles, text, handwriting and attachments. Slide PDFs import for highlights, underlines and handwriting on the same page. Questions from the left column can become flashcards and cloze cards reviewed on an FSRS spaced-repetition schedule, and audio recorded in class stays attached to the page where it started, so it plays back with that page's notes.
look: Whether it can search your own handwriting, and whether that works offline
Whether slide PDFs import into the same notebook as your notes and take writing on top
Whether a ruler or shape tool lets you draw the page division and reuse it
Whether nested folders and tags separate subjects and terms
Whether it needs an account, shows ads, and whether it is monthly or a one-time purchase
steps: Create one notebook or folder per subject and write the meaning of your three colours on its first page.
On every new page, print the heading in block capitals at the top and draw the one-third left column with the ruler.
Import the slide PDF before class; during class write only what the lecturer adds, beside the slide or on the right side of the page.
The same day after class, write a question in the left column for each section of content and a two-sentence summary at the bottom.
Every weekend, cover the right side and answer the left column; turn anything you cannot answer into a review card, then search a handwritten word to confirm the app finds it.
rows: Whether heading, question column and summary box are all there
If every page looks different, revision time goes on working out what matters

A colour whose meaning keeps changing becomes decoration and does nothing at exam time
Whether slide PDFs and the notes you wrote are in the same notebook
In separate apps you switch back and forth during revision and usually read only one side
en.fits: 100 Notes Studio fits students who write by hand on iPad and want notes, slide PDFs, class audio and flashcards in one notebook with no account and no monthly fee. It does not fit anyone who needs to edit notes with classmates in real time or sync through the cloud across platforms. The free version has the full set of writing tools and one notebook with unlimited pages; a one-time purchase unlocks the rest.
faq: How many colours should I use in my notes?
Three: a main colour, one for definitions and likely exam material, one for your own questions. Keep the meanings the same in every subject; more than that and you forget which colour means what.
If the lecturer already gives slides as a PDF, do I still need to write by hand?
Yes, but only what the lecturer adds and your own questions. Import the slides into the notebook and write beside them or on the next page; what is already printed does not need copying.
Is 100 Notes Studio a monthly subscription?

No. The free version includes 29 writing tools, PDF markup, page audio, handwriting search and study mode, with 1 active notebook of up to 5 pages and 2 of the 100 styles. A one-time purchase adds more notebooks, all 100 styles, vector PDF export, version history and encrypted backup. No account, no ads.

loc.title: claude 用量：工作、個人或 Pro、Max 多個帳號，下一個該用哪個
loc.meta: 同時有好幾個 Claude 帳號時，要看的不是哪個剩得多，而是哪個先重置。把每個帳號的 5 小時與每週額度、確切重置時間排在同一個小工具上，換帳號就不用一個個登入查。
loc.h1: claude 用量：多個帳號時，先看哪個先重置
loc.lead: 一個帳號額度見底，手上還有另一個帳號，卻不知道哪個撐得比較久，這是多帳號的人常卡住的地方。
loc.answer: 有多個 Claude 帳號時，把每個帳號的 5 小時額度、每週額度和確切重置時間並排，再依 5 小時重置時間排序，下一個要接手的帳號就會排在前面，不必逐一登入查看。
paras: 搜尋 claude 用量的人，很多手上不只一個帳號：公司給的工作帳號、自己付費的個人帳號，或是 Pro 和 Max 各一個。問題是每個帳號的 5 小時工作階段額度和每週額度各自倒數，剩得多的帳號不一定撐得久；每週額度快見底的帳號，就算 5 小時額度還很滿，也可能做到一半就停。所以比較帳號時，要同時看兩種額度和各自的重置時間。
UsageNow 把所有帳號放在同一個畫面：工作與個人、Pro 與 Max 並排顯示，可以依 5 小時重置時間、每週重置時間、用量由高到低或由低到高、名稱或服務排序，也能拖移成自己的順序。主畫面與鎖定畫面小工具上可以直接翻看每個帳號，想看最新數字時，點一下小工具就會更新。
換帳號的時機也能交給提醒：替 5 小時額度、每週額度或所有額度設定你在意的百分比，例如 90 或 98，每個額度在每個週期只提醒一次；再開啟重置提醒，原本見底的帳號一恢復就知道可以切回去。登入都在各服務自己的官方登入頁面完成，登入資訊只留在裝置的鑰匙圈，沒有 UsageNow 伺服器，也不需要另外註冊帳號。

en.title: Claude usage across several accounts: which one to continue on
en.meta: With several Claude accounts, the one with more left is not always the one that lasts. Line up each account's 5-hour and weekly limits and exact reset times on one widget, and switching stops being guesswork.
en.h1: Claude usage with several accounts: look at which one resets first
en.lead: One account is out, another still has room, and you cannot tell which will last longer. That is where people with several accounts get stuck.
en.answer: With several Claude accounts, put each account's 5-hour limit, weekly limit and exact reset time side by side and sort by 5-hour reset; the account to continue on comes up first, without signing in to each one.
paras: Many people searching for Claude usage run more than one account: a work account from the company, a personal one they pay for, or a Pro and a Max side by side. Each account counts down its 5-hour session limit and weekly limit separately, so the account with more left is not always the one that lasts. An account near its weekly cap can stop you halfway even with a full 5-hour window, which is why comparing accounts means reading both limits and both reset times.

UsageNow puts every account on one screen: work and personal, Pro and Max, side by side, sorted by 5-hour reset, weekly reset, highest or lowest usage, name or service, or dragged into your own order. On Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets you can flip through each account directly, and a tap on the widget refreshes it when you want the latest numbers.

The moment to switch can come from an alert instead of memory. Set the percentage you care about, like 90 or 98, for the 5-hour limit, the weekly limit or all limits; each alert fires once per limit and cycle. Turn on the reset alert and you know when the account that ran out is back. Sign-in happens on each service's own login page and stays in the device's Keychain; there is no UsageNow server and no account to create.

Turn on the reset alert and switch back as soon as a limit returns.

paras: 클로드 사용량을 검색하는 분 중에는 Claude Code 같은 도구로 긴 작업을 돌리다 갑자기 멈춘 경험이 있는 개발자가 많습니다. Claude는 5시간 세션 한도와 주간 한도가 따로 돌아가고 모델별 주간 한도까지 있어서, 어느 쪽에 먼저 닿을지 예측하기 어렵습니다. 그렇다고 몇 분마다 사용량을 열어 보는 것은 지키려던 집중을 스스로 깨는 일입니다.

그래서 확인하는 대신 알림을 받는 쪽이 낫습니다. UsageNow에서는 5시간 한도, 주간 한도 또는 모든 한도를 고른 뒤 신경 쓰이는 퍼센트를 직접 입력해 알림을 만들 수 있고, 원하는 만큼 추가할 수 있습니다. 알림은 한도별로 주기마다 한 번만 울리므로 잠금 화면이 알림으로 가득 차지 않습니다. 예를 들어 90에서는 지금 단계를 정리할 시점을, 98에서는 지금까지의 작업을 커밋할 시점을 알리게 둘 수 있습니다.
멈춘 뒤에는 초기화 알림이 다시 시작할 때를 알려 줍니다. 초기화까지 남은 시간은 홈 화면·잠금 화면 위젯과 Apple Watch 컴플리케이션에서 실시간으로 카운트다운되고, 정확한 초기화 시각도 사용자 지역 형식으로 표시됩니다. 로그인은 각 서비스의 공식 로그인 페이지에서 하며, 로그인 정보는 기기의 키체인에만 보관됩니다.

An alert is the better habit. In UsageNow you choose the 5-hour limit, the weekly limit or all limits, type the percentage that matters to you and add as many alerts as you like. Sign-in happens on each service's official login page and stays only in the device's Keychain.

loc.h1: 待辦事項 App 總是用不久？挑一個你每天會打開的
loc.lead: 下載了好幾個待辦事項 App 卻都沒在用，通常不是你不夠自律，而是那個 App 沒有讓你想打開它。
loc.answer: 看得到、打勾有感覺、每天只放幾件事——同時做到這三件事的待辦清單，才會被每天打開；功能多寡反而是次要的。
paras: 第一個條件是看得到。藏在第三頁資料夾裡的 App，再好用也會被忘記。把今天的清單放到主畫面小工具，每次解鎖手機就會看到，等於每天自動提醒自己好幾次，不必再靠記性去打開它。
第二個條件是完成有感覺。劃掉一行、點一下圓圈、進度往前走，這些小回饋是每天願意回來的理由。外觀也算在內：主畫面是粉嫩色系，放一個灰色表格風的 App 會很突兀，有喜歡的主題，才會願意讓小工具一直留在那裡。
第三個條件是每天的量要小。清單越寫越長，就會從工具變成罪惡感來源。每天只放四、五件真的要做的事，其他的另外放一份清單，週末再看。Mochi 就是照這個想法做的：輕點小圓圈完成打勾，有 101 款主題、桌面小工具和 Apple Watch App；免費版可以有 2 個清單、每個最多 4 個項目。

en.title: To-do list app you stop using? Pick one you keep opening
en.meta: A to-do list app gets abandoned when it is out of sight, finishing feels like nothing and the list keeps growing. Check the widget, the tick and a daily cap. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: Stopped using every to-do list app? Pick one you keep opening
en.lead: If you have installed several to-do list apps and use none of them, the issue is usually not discipline. The app simply never made you want to open it.
en.answer: Visible, satisfying to tick, and small enough to finish each day: a to-do list that does all three gets opened daily. The number of features matters far less.
paras: The first condition is visibility. An app buried in a folder on page three gets forgotten, however good it is. Put today's list in a Home Screen widget and you see it every time you unlock your phone, which is several reminders a day without relying on memory.

The second is a finish that feels like something. Crossing out a line, tapping a circle, watching progress move: these small returns are why people come back. Looks count too. On a pastel Home Screen, a grey spreadsheet-style app sticks out, and a theme you like is a reason to keep the widget there.

The third is a small daily list. A list that only grows turns from a tool into a source of guilt. Keep four or five things you will really do today and park the rest on a second list for the weekend. Mochi is built around that idea: tap the little circle to check off, 101 themes, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch; the free version has 2 lists of up to 4 tasks each.

Start with four. Finishing four feels better than crossing four out of twenty, and it makes opening the list tomorrow easier.

loc.title: 小一注音闖關前在家怎麼複習？認讀、拼讀、聲調三件事的練法
loc.meta: 小一注音教學期快結束時，不少學校會用闖關或小考確認孩子學會了沒。在家不用出考卷：把認讀、拼讀、聲調拆開，每天各練幾分鐘就夠。文末說明 Lumi注音星球 可以接在哪一步。
loc.h1: 小一注音闖關前，在家怎麼複習認讀、拼讀與聲調
loc.lead: 注音教學期的尾聲，不少學校會用闖關、小考或朗讀確認孩子的程度。在家複習不必模擬考試，把要確認的三件事拆開，每天各練一小段，孩子比較不會緊張。
loc.answer: 把複習拆成認讀、拼讀、聲調三件事，每天各練三到四分鐘：先聽音找符號，再拼兩三個音，最後同一個音連唸四聲。
paras: 認讀是看到符號唸得出來、聽到聲音找得到符號。容易混的通常是長得像或聲音接近的組合，例如ㄅ和ㄆ、ㄓ和ㄗ、ㄣ和ㄥ。複習時不用把 37 個從頭唸到尾，挑孩子這週最常錯的三到五個就好。
拼讀是把聲母、介音、韻母接成一個音，例如ㄒ、ㄧ、ㄠ接起來是ㄒㄧㄠ。孩子如果每個符號都認得卻拼不出來，先放慢：大人唸一個音，孩子指出它由哪幾個符號組成，再反過來讓孩子自己拼。
聲調最容易在闖關時被抓出來，尤其是二聲和三聲。同一個音連唸四聲（ㄇㄚ：媽、麻、馬、罵）再配手勢比高低，比單獨背調號有用。Lumi注音星球 的四種玩法剛好對應這幾步，可以免費開始使用。

en.title: Learn Zhuyin for kids: a 10-minute home review of symbols, blending and tones
en.meta: Near the end of the first-grade Zhuyin unit in Taiwan, many schools check reading, blending and tones. At home you don't need a mock test: practise each skill for a few minutes a day. A routine, and where Lumi Bopomofo fits.
en.h1: Learn Zhuyin for kids: reviewing symbols, blending and tones at home
en.lead: Toward the end of the Zhuyin unit, many Taiwanese schools check progress with a short quiz, a reading or a game-style challenge. Families anywhere can use the same three checks at home without turning practice into a test.
en.answer: Split review into three skills (reading symbols, blending and tones) and spend three or four minutes on each: find the symbol for a sound, blend two or three syllables, then say one syllable in all four tones.
paras: Reading means saying a symbol when you see it and finding it when you hear it. Mix-ups usually come in look-alike or sound-alike pairs such as ㄅ and ㄆ, ㄓ and ㄗ, or ㄣ and ㄥ. You don't need to run through all 37 symbols; pick the three to five your child missed most this week.

Blending joins an initial, a medial and a final into one syllable: ㄒ, ㄧ and ㄠ become ㄒㄧㄠ. If a child knows every symbol but can't blend, slow down: you say a syllable, they point to the symbols inside it, then swap roles and let them build it.

Tones are where most mistakes show up, especially the second and third tones. Saying one syllable in all four tones (ㄇㄚ: mā, má, mǎ, mà) with a hand gesture for the pitch works better than memorising tone marks. Lumi Bopomofo's four games map onto these steps, and it is free to start.

Finish with a minute of whatever practice your child picks, and start tomorrow with today's misses.

faq: What if my child didn't pass the school's Zhuyin check?

Work out which kind of mistake it was: not recognising symbols, not blending, or wrong tones. Each needs different practice, and a few minutes a day on the weakest one usually helps more than redoing everything.
How long should we practise each day?
For a first grader, about ten minutes at a regular time is plenty. Short and daily beats long and occasional.

loc.h1: 爸媽自己注音不熟，怎麼陪孩子練注音？
loc.lead: 很多大人的注音是小時候學的，多年沒用，聲調和相近的音難免不確定。陪練的重點不是大人發音標準，而是每天陪孩子聽、找、拼一小段。
loc.answer: 大人不用當發音示範：讓孩子聽標準的音、自己找出符號再拼起來，大人負責陪伴、計時，記下孩子常錯的音就好。
paras: 大人最常不確定的，多半是相近的音：ㄓㄔㄕ和ㄗㄘㄙ、ㄣ和ㄥ，還有二聲和三聲。這很正常，日常說話本來就常混著唸。與其擔心自己唸錯、教錯，不如把示範發音交給老師、課本附的音檔或有語音的練習工具。
大人可以做的事反而更重要：固定每天的時段、一次只練幾分鐘、把孩子常錯的音記下來，隔天先複習。孩子唸錯時先別急著糾正，讓他再聽一次正確的音、自己比比看，比較不會讓練習變成壓力。
如果學校或安親班有注音練習本，可以照它的順序走，在家只要補上「聽」和「拼」的次數。Lumi注音星球 會播放聲音讓孩子選出正確的注音，也有拼音、聲調和筆順的練習，可以免費開始使用。

孩子能不能自己操作，大人只要在旁邊陪
聽辨、拼讀、聲調和筆順有沒有分開練
會不會跳出廣告或外部連結
需不需要註冊帳號、會不會收集孩子的資料
steps: 先看聯絡簿或問老師，確認班上正在教哪幾個符號。
每天固定一個 10 分鐘的時段，例如功課寫完、洗澡前。
示範發音交給音檔或有語音的練習工具，大人只負責陪孩子聽、找、拼。
把孩子當天唸錯的音記在小卡上，隔天先從這幾個開始。
自己不確定的音，查教育部《國語注音符號手冊》確認，不用硬猜。
rows: 大人不確定時交給音檔或工具，孩子每次聽到的音才一致
每天固定的時段與長度
固定比拉長有用，孩子比較不會抗拒
有沒有記下來、隔天先複習
重複練錯的那幾個，比 37 個重來一遍省時間
loc.fits: Lumi注音星球（Lumi Bopomofo）適合想陪練、但對自己發音沒把握的爸媽：餵食小夥伴讓孩子聽聲音選出正確的注音，拼音小火車、聲調雲霄飛車、魔法描寫分別練拼讀、四聲和筆順。完全無廣告、不蒐集任何個人資料、無需註冊，進度只存在裝置本機。
faq: 我自己注音也不太會，可以教孩子嗎？
可以。大人的角色是陪伴和安排練習，不必是發音最標準的人；示範交給音檔或有語音的工具，不確定的音再查教育部的注音符號手冊。
孩子唸錯時要馬上糾正嗎？
不一定。先讓孩子再聽一次正確的音、自己比比看，常比直接糾正更有效，也比較不會讓練習變成壓力。
Lumi注音星球 只有中文介面嗎？
不是，介面是中英雙語，海外華人家庭也適用。

en.title: How to teach my child Zhuyin when I can't read it myself
en.meta: Many parents abroad want their child to read Zhuyin (Bopomofo) but never learned it, or forgot it. You don't need to model the sounds yourself: how to practise together, and where Lumi Bopomofo fits.
en.h1: How to teach your child Zhuyin when you can't read it yourself
en.lead: Plenty of parents, especially outside Taiwan, never learned Zhuyin or learned it decades ago. Your job isn't to pronounce every sound perfectly; it's to build a short daily habit of listening, finding and blending.
en.answer: You don't need to be the pronunciation model: let your child hear correct audio, find the symbols and blend them, while you keep time, keep it light and note the sounds they miss.
paras: The sounds adults are least sure about are usually the close pairs (ㄓㄔㄕ versus ㄗㄘㄙ, ㄣ versus ㄥ) and the second versus the third tone. Instead of worrying about teaching them wrong, hand the modelling to recordings: a teacher, a textbook's audio or a practice app with sound.

What you add matters more: a fixed time each day, a few minutes per session, and a list of the sounds your child missed so tomorrow starts with them. When your child gets one wrong, play the correct sound again and let them compare before you correct.

If your child attends a weekend Chinese school, follow its order and add more listening and blending at home. Lumi Bopomofo plays a sound and lets your child pick the right symbol, and has games for blending, tones and stroke order. It is free to start, and the interface is in English and Chinese.
look: Whether the practice has clear audio your child can replay
Whether your child can use it alone while you sit beside them
Whether listening, blending, tones and tracing are practised separately
Whether ads or outside links pop up
Whether it needs an account or collects your child's data
steps: Ask the teacher which symbols the class is on, so home practice matches.
Pick one fixed ten-minute slot a day, for example after dinner.
Let recordings or an app with audio model the sounds; you listen, find and blend with your child.
Write down today's missed sounds and start tomorrow with them.
Check any sound you're unsure of in the Taiwan Ministry of Education's Mandarin Phonetic Symbols handbook instead of guessing.
rows: If it isn't you, your child hears the same correct sound every time
A fixed daily slot and length
Regular beats long, and children resist less
Whether they're noted and reviewed first
Repeating the few misses saves going through all 37
en.fits: Lumi Bopomofo suits parents who want to help but aren't sure of the sounds: Feed the Friends lets your child listen and pick the right symbol, while Sound Train, Tone Coaster and Magic Tracing cover blending, the four tones and strokes. Completely ad-free, collects no personal data, no sign-up, progress stays on the device.
faq: Can I teach Zhuyin if I can't read it?
Yes. Your role is to organise the practice and keep it going, not to be the most accurate speaker. Let recordings model the sounds and check anything unclear in the Ministry of Education handbook.
Should I correct every mistake straight away?
Not always. Playing the correct sound again and letting your child compare often works better than direct correction, and keeps practice from feeling like pressure.
Does Lumi Bopomofo have an English interface?
Yes. The interface is in English and Chinese, so parents who don't read Chinese can follow along.

loc.title: Metas de ano novo: da lista bonita ao checklist que passa de janeiro
loc.meta: Lista de metas de ano novo costuma morrer antes do Carnaval. Transforme cada meta em uma ação diária de 10 minutos e revise só aos domingos. Passo a passo.
loc.h1: Metas de ano novo: como transformar a lista em um checklist diário que sobrevive a janeiro
loc.lead: Escrever as metas na virada é fácil. O difícil é que "ler 20 livros" ou "entrar em forma" não diz o que fazer numa terça-feira qualquer de janeiro, com calor, férias das crianças e a fatura do cartão chegando.
loc.answer: Para cada meta, escreva uma ação que caiba em 10 minutos e que dê para marcar como feita hoje. Deixe no máximo três dessas ações no checklist do dia e revise a lista inteira só uma vez por semana.
paras: Meta não é tarefa. "Economizar" é um resultado; "anotar o gasto do dia antes de dormir" é algo que você marca ou não marca. A regra prática: se não dá para dizer, às 22h, se aquilo foi feito hoje, ainda não está pronto para entrar no checklist. Reescreva até virar um verbo concreto com um objeto concreto.

Janeiro no Brasil é o mês mais traiçoeiro para começar: viagem, praia, rotina bagunçada e a volta ao trabalho só depois do dia 5 ou 10. Em vez de começar com tudo no dia 1º, defina a versão mínima de cada ação (5 páginas, 10 minutos de caminhada) para os dias fora de casa e a versão normal para quando a rotina voltar. Quem só tem a versão "ideal" costuma desistir na primeira semana de viagem.

O que mantém o checklist vivo é ele estar à vista e ser rápido de marcar. O Mochi é um checklist simples: você escreve a tarefa e toca no pequeno círculo quando conclui, com lembretes, acompanhamento de hábitos e rotina, widgets na Tela de Início e acesso pelo Apple Watch. A versão gratuita inclui 2 listas com até 4 tarefas cada — o suficiente para uma lista "hoje" com três ações e uma de revisão.

Reescreva cada uma como ação de 10 minutos com verbo concreto (ex.: "caminhar 10 min depois do almoço").
Coloque as três ações no checklist do dia com lembrete em horário fixo.
Todo domingo de janeiro, veja o que você marcou: ação que falhou 4 vezes na semana fica menor, não é abandonada.

Para o checklist diário, três. Você pode ter mais metas no papel, mas só três ações por dia — acima disso, a taxa de conclusão cai e a lista vira cobrança.
E se eu falhar a primeira semana?
Diminua a ação em vez de recomeçar do zero. Trocar 30 minutos por 10 mantém o hábito vivo; esperar a "segunda-feira perfeita" geralmente empurra tudo para depois do Carnaval.

Sim. A versão gratuita inclui 2 listas com até 4 tarefas cada, que cabem uma lista do dia com três ações e uma lista de revisão.

en.title: New Year's resolutions list into a daily checklist that survives January
en.meta: Most New Year's resolution lists are dead by February. Turn each goal into one 10-minute action you can tick today, cap it at three a day, and review weekly.
en.h1: New Year's resolutions: turn the list into a daily checklist that lasts past January
en.lead: Writing resolutions on December 31 is easy. The problem is that "read more" or "get fit" tells you nothing about what to do on a cold Tuesday in mid-January.
en.answer: Rewrite each resolution as one action that takes about 10 minutes and can be ticked off today. Keep no more than three of those on the daily checklist, and review the whole list only once a week.
paras: A resolution is an outcome; a checklist item is something you either did or didn't do today. Test each one at 10 p.m.: if you can't answer yes or no, it isn't ready for the list. Rewrite it until it's a specific verb with a specific object — "walk 10 minutes after lunch", not "exercise more".

The first two weeks of January are full of travel, leftover holiday plans and a messy routine. Give every action a minimum version (two pages, a five-minute walk) for chaotic days and a normal version for regular days. People who only have the ideal version usually quit the first time a day goes sideways.

What keeps a checklist alive is seeing it and ticking it fast. Mochi is a simple checklist: write a task and tap the little circle when it's done, with reminders, habit and routine tracking, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each — enough for a three-item "today" list plus a review list.
look: Each resolution has an action you can tick today
No more than three actions per day
A minimum version for travel or chaotic days
A fixed reminder time, not "whenever"
One weekly slot to review and cut
steps: By December 31, write every resolution down without filtering.
Pick three; move the rest to a "maybe in March" list.
Rewrite each as a 10-minute action with a concrete verb.
Put the three actions on your daily checklist with a reminder at a fixed time.
Every Sunday in January, check what you ticked: an action missed four times that week gets smaller, not dropped.
en.fits: Mochi suits anyone who wants a light checklist for three daily actions: write, tap the circle when done, get a reminder, and see the list on a widget or Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists of up to 4 tasks; Premium, an in-app purchase, unlocks unlimited lists and tasks.
faq: How many resolutions should I have?
Three on the daily checklist. You can keep more on paper, but more than three daily actions usually turns the list into a guilt reminder.
What if I miss the first week?
Shrink the action instead of restarting. Swapping 30 minutes for 10 keeps the habit alive; waiting for a perfect Monday usually pushes it to spring.
Can I set this up in Mochi for free?
Yes. The free version includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each, which fits a three-action daily list and a review list.

term: 大掃除 チェックリスト

loc.title: 大掃除チェックリスト｜部屋別・日にち別に分けて年末に終わらせる
loc.meta: 年末の大掃除は「全部を一日で」が失敗のもと。12月上旬から部屋別・日にち別に分け、1日1か所ずつ片づける段取りとチェックリストの作り方をまとめました。
loc.h1: 大掃除チェックリスト：部屋別×日にち別に分けて、仕事納め前から少しずつ
loc.lead: 大掃除が終わらない理由は、やる気よりも段取りです。12月29日から年末年始の休みに入って、そこで家じゅうを一気に片づけようとすると、買い出しや帰省の準備とぶつかって半分も終わりません。
loc.answer: 大掃除は「部屋ごと」に項目を書き出し、12月上旬から1日1か所・30分以内に割り振ります。寒くて水仕事がつらい窓やベランダは暖かい日中の週末に、キッチンの換気扇など時間がかかる場所は早めに、玄関は最後に回すのが基本です。
paras: 昔から12月13日は「正月事始め」とされ、煤払いを始める日とされてきました。2026年は日曜日なので、この日に全体のリストを作るのにちょうどいい区切りです。ここから12月28日（月）の仕事納めの週までに、平日は1日30分で終わる小さな場所、週末はキッチンや窓などの大物、という配分にすると無理がありません。
リストは「キッチン」「浴室」「リビング」「玄関」のように部屋ごとに分け、さらに「換気扇のフィルター」「窓のサッシ」のように手を動かす単位まで細かくします。「キッチンを掃除する」では終わったかどうか判断できませんが、「コンロの五徳をつけ置き」なら30分後にチェックを入れられます。上から下へ、奥から手前へ、の順番で並べておくと、終わったところを汚し直さずに済みます。
部屋ごとのリストをスマホで分けて持っておくと、今日の分だけを見て動けます。Mochiはやることを書いて、終わったら小さな丸をタップするシンプルなチェックリストアプリで、リマインダー、ホーム画面のウィジェット、Apple Watchでの確認にも対応しています。無料版ではリスト2つ（各4項目まで）が使え、プレミアム（App内課金）ではリストと項目が無制限になります。
look: 項目が「部屋」と「作業単位」まで分かれているか
1項目が30分以内で終わる大きさになっているか
窓・ベランダなど外回りを暖かい日中に入れているか
洗剤・ゴミ袋の買い出しを最初の項目にしているか
粗大ごみ・資源ごみの年内最終回収日を確認したか
steps: 12月13日（日）までに、部屋ごとに掃除したい場所を全部書き出す。
それぞれを「30分で終わる作業」に分け、時間がかかる順に並べる。
お住まいの自治体の年内最後のごみ収集日を確認し、捨てる物の仕分けを先にやる。
平日は1日1項目、週末は換気扇・窓・冷蔵庫などの大物を割り振る。
12月29日以降は玄関と水回りの仕上げだけにして、30日までに終える。

en.title: Year-end deep cleaning checklist split by room and by day
en.meta: Trying to deep-clean the whole home in one weekend before the holidays rarely works. Split the checklist by room, then into 30-minute jobs spread over December.
en.h1: Year-end deep cleaning checklist: split it by room, then by day
en.lead: Deep cleaning stalls because of planning, not motivation. Leave everything for the last days of December and it collides with shopping, travel and guests.
en.answer: List every job room by room, break each into a task that takes 30 minutes or less, and spread them across December — one small job on weekdays, big jobs like the oven hood and windows on weekends, the entryway last.
paras: Start the list in mid-December, not the week of Christmas. Weekdays get small jobs you can finish in 30 minutes (one cupboard, one bathroom drawer), weekends get the jobs that need time and daylight, such as windows, the range hood filter or the fridge. Put outdoor jobs on the warmest afternoons you can.

Split the list by room first — kitchen, bathroom, living room, entryway — and then into concrete actions: "soak the stove grates" instead of "clean the kitchen". You can tick the first one after 30 minutes; the second never feels finished. Order each room top to bottom and back to front so you don't re-dirty what you just cleaned.

Keeping one list per room on your phone lets you look at only today's job. Mochi is a simple checklist app: write a task and tap the little circle when it's done, with reminders, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each, and Premium (an in-app purchase) unlocks unlimited lists and tasks.

faq: When should I start year-end cleaning?
About two weeks before the holiday. At 30 minutes a day that covers most homes without a marathon weekend.
Which order is most efficient?
Top to bottom, back to front: lights and hood first, floors and the entryway last, so dust doesn't fall onto finished areas.

loc.title: 새해 목표 체크리스트: 1월 1일과 설날, 두 번의 시작으로 나누기
loc.meta: 새해 목표가 작심삼일로 끝나는 건 목표가 너무 커서입니다. 1월 1일부터 설날(2027년 2월 6일)까지 5주를 1차 구간으로 잡고 매일 체크할 행동으로 바꾸는 법.
loc.h1: 새해 목표 체크리스트: 작심삼일 대신 설날까지 5주 버티는 법
loc.lead: ‘운동하기’, ‘영어 공부’, ‘돈 모으기’. 매년 비슷한 목표를 적지만 1월 둘째 주쯤이면 다이어리는 비어 있습니다. 의지가 약해서가 아니라, 오늘 무엇을 하면 체크할 수 있는지가 정해져 있지 않아서입니다.
loc.answer: 목표 하나마다 ‘오늘 10분 안에 끝나고 체크할 수 있는 행동’을 하나씩 정하고, 하루 체크리스트에는 최대 3개만 올리세요. 그리고 1월 1일부터 설날(2027년 2월 6일)까지를 1차 구간으로 잡아, 설 연휴에 한 번 점검하고 다시 시작합니다.
paras: 한국에는 새해가 두 번 있습니다. 양력 1월 1일에 시작해서 무너졌다면, 설날이 자연스러운 두 번째 출발점이 됩니다. 2027년 설날은 2월 6일(토)이라, 1월 1일부터 약 5주가 1차 구간입니다. 1년짜리 목표를 5주 단위로 끊으면 ‘이번 구간에 몇 번 체크했나’를 보고 다음 구간에서 행동을 키우거나 줄일 수 있습니다.

체크리스트에 들어갈 항목은 결과가 아니라 행동이어야 합니다. ‘살 빼기’는 체크할 수 없지만 ‘퇴근 후 계단으로 올라가기’는 오늘 밤 체크할 수 있습니다. 밤 10시에 ‘했다/안 했다’로 답할 수 없는 항목은 아직 목표 상태이니 동사와 대상이 분명해질 때까지 다시 쓰세요. 야근이나 회식이 있는 날을 위해 ‘최소 버전’(단어 5개, 스트레칭 3분)도 함께 적어 두면 연속 기록이 끊기지 않습니다.

체크리스트는 자주 눈에 띄고 바로 체크할 수 있어야 오래 갑니다. Mochi는 할 일을 적고 끝나면 작은 동그라미를 탭하는 간단한 체크리스트 앱으로, 알림, 습관 및 루틴 트래킹, 홈 화면 위젯, Apple Watch 지원이 있습니다. 무료 버전에서는 목록 2개(목록당 항목 최대 4개)를 쓸 수 있어 ‘오늘의 3가지’ 목록과 점검용 목록을 만들기에 충분합니다.

en.title: New Year goals checklist: use January 1 and Lunar New Year as two starts
en.meta: New Year goals fail when they're too big to tick. Treat January 1 to Lunar New Year (Feb 6, 2027) as a five-week first round of small daily actions.
en.h1: New Year goals checklist: plan a five-week first round, not a whole year
en.lead: "Exercise", "learn a language", "save money" — the same goals every year, and by mid-January the planner is blank. Usually it's not willpower; it's that nothing on the list can be ticked today.
en.answer: Give each goal one action that takes about 10 minutes and can be checked off today, keep at most three on the daily checklist, and treat January 1 to Lunar New Year (February 6, 2027) as a first round you review and restart.
paras: A year is too long to steer by. Cutting it into rounds — January 1 to Lunar New Year is about five weeks in 2027 — lets you look at how often you actually ticked each action and adjust before the habit quietly dies. If January went badly, the second new year is a natural restart rather than a failure.

Checklist items must be actions, not outcomes. "Lose weight" can't be ticked; "take the stairs after work" can be ticked tonight. If you can't answer yes or no at 10 p.m., rewrite it. Add a minimum version (three words of vocabulary, a three-minute stretch) for late-work days so the streak doesn't break.

Checklists last when they're visible and quick to tick. Mochi is a simple checklist app: write a task and tap the little circle when it's done, with reminders, habit and routine tracking, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each — enough for a "today's three" list and a review list.

Three or fewer daily items

Pick three and move the rest to an "after round one" list.
Turn each into a 10-minute action plus a minimum version.

Around February 6, review five weeks of ticks: grow what worked, shrink what didn't, start round two.
en.fits: Mochi suits people who want to shrink New Year goals to "today's three" and tap a circle as each is done, with reminders, habit tracking, widgets and Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists of up to 4 tasks; Premium (in-app purchase) unlocks unlimited.
faq: How many goals should go on the daily list?
Three or fewer. You can hold more goals, but more daily items tends to turn the checklist into pressure.
I already fell off in January. Now what?
Use Lunar New Year as a second start and make the action smaller instead of restarting at full size.
Is Mochi's free version enough?
It includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each, which fits a three-action daily list and a review list. Premium unlocks unlimited lists and tasks.

loc.title: 跨年倒數計畫：從 12/31 往回推，該訂的票、該做的事一次排好
loc.meta: 跨年要看煙火、出遊或回家，最怕到 12 月底才發現車票、餐廳、住宿都沒了。從 12/31 往回推出每一步的截止日，照著做就不會漏。
loc.h1: 跨年倒數計畫：從 12 月 31 日往回推，每一步什麼時候要做完
loc.lead: 跨年最常見的遺憾不是當晚不好玩，而是事前少做了一件事：回程車票沒搶到、想去的餐廳早就訂滿、住宿只剩很貴的房型。2026 年的 12/31 是星期四，隔天 1/1 元旦放假，想看煙火又想出遊的人特別多。
loc.answer: 先把「12/31 晚上要在哪裡、怎麼回家」定下來，再從這天往回推：大約前 4 週處理住宿與長途車票，前 2 週訂餐廳和確認人數，前 1 週查交通管制與接駁，前 1 天備好隨身物品。每一步都寫上截止日，比只看「還剩幾天」更不容易漏。
paras: 倒數計畫的重點是「截止日」而不是「剩幾天」。只看離跨年還有 26 天，很容易覺得時間很多；但如果寫成「12/3 前要訂好回程車票」「12/17 前要確認餐廳人數」，每一步都有自己的期限，哪一件已經拖到就一目了然。高鐵、台鐵通常在乘車日前約 4 週開放訂票，熱門日子的票開賣後很快就會被訂走，元旦當天的回程票尤其要記得。
看煙火的人要特別把交通算進去。大型跨年場地周邊常有交通管制，捷運也可能延長營運或改成管制出入口，這些資訊多半在活動前一到兩週才公布。與其當天現查，不如在計畫裡排一個「12/24 查交管與接駁公告」的步驟；要帶長輩或小孩的話，也順便決定結束後是要等人潮散去，還是提早離場。
把這些步驟放進同一個倒數裡，比散在備忘錄和聊天紀錄裡可靠。CountDaysNow 的副標就是「Countdown Plan: Work Backwards」，可以替一個事件設定事前準備步驟，並顯示哪些已逾期、今天到期或 7 天內到期；剩 7 天、3 天、1 天和當天也會提醒，事件可以放在主畫面小工具、鎖定畫面與動態島。免費版最多 3 個進行中事件，無廣告、無訂閱、不需帳號。

高鐵、台鐵通常在乘車日前約 4 週開放訂票，實際開賣時間以各家公告為準。元旦當天的回程是熱門時段，建議開賣當天就處理。
看跨年煙火要提早多久到？

en.title: New Year's Eve countdown plan: work backwards from December 31
en.meta: New Year's Eve goes wrong weeks earlier: no train seats, full restaurants, pricey rooms. Work backwards from Dec 31 and give every step a due date.
en.h1: New Year's Eve countdown plan: work backwards from December 31
en.lead: Most New Year's Eve regrets come from something skipped weeks earlier — the train home sold out, the restaurant fully booked, only expensive rooms left. In 2026, December 31 falls on a Thursday.
en.answer: Decide where you'll be on the night and how you'll get home, then work backwards: lodging and long-distance tickets about four weeks out, restaurant and headcount two weeks out, road closures and transit one week out, the go-bag the day before. Give each step a due date, not just a countdown.
paras: A countdown plan is about due dates, not days remaining. "26 days to go" feels like plenty; "book the train home by December 3" doesn't. Once every step has its own deadline, it's obvious which one is slipping. Long-distance trains often open bookings about four weeks ahead, and January 1 return trips go fast.

If you're going to a fireworks show, plan the trip out as carefully as the trip in. Big events usually come with road closures and transit changes that are announced only a week or two before. Schedule a step to check those announcements, and decide in advance whether you'll leave early or wait out the crowd if you're with kids or older relatives.

Keeping every step under one countdown beats scattering them across notes and chats. CountDaysNow's Countdown Plan lets you give an event its own preparation steps a set number of days before it, and shows what's late, due today and due in the next 7 days; alerts arrive 7, 3 and 1 day before and on the day, and the countdown can live on widgets, the Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island. Countdown Plan is free, works on-device and needs no account.

Many long-distance trains open about four weeks before departure; check your operator's notice. January 1 returns are in high demand, so book when sales open.

loc.lead: 2026年のクリスマスイブは木曜日、クリスマスは金曜日。平日なので、当日にあわてて準備する余裕はほとんどありません。しかも年末は年賀状や大掃除、仕事納めの準備まで重なります。

en.meta: Christmas prep is about "by when", not "how many days left". A schedule worked back from Dec 25 for cake and dinner bookings, gift shipping and cards.
en.h1: Christmas countdown prep: a schedule worked back from December 25
en.lead: In 2026 Christmas Eve is a Thursday and Christmas Day a Friday — both workdays for many people, so there's little room for last-minute prep.
en.answer: Set December 25 as the finish line, then book cake and dinner in late November, order gifts in early December, decorate and send cards mid-December, and confirm pickups the day before. Count down to each earlier deadline, not just to the 25th.
paras: Popular bakeries and restaurants fill up for December 24 and 25 well before the day, and some order windows close once they hit capacity. Decide in November, and fix the pickup time too — if the 24th is a workday, check you can actually get there.

Gifts should be planned from the date they need to arrive. Shipping slows in December, and gift-wrapping or engraving adds days. If you're mailing to family far away, order while delivery by the 24th is still guaranteed. Holiday cards and New Year cards have their own cutoffs that land the same week.

With several deadlines, seeing the finish line and the steps before it together cuts mistakes. CountDaysNow counts down to the dates ahead, with alerts 7, 3 and 1 day before and on the day, and shows the countdown on Home Screen widgets, the Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island. Its Countdown Plan gives an event preparation steps and shows what's late, due today and due in the next 7 days. No ads, no subscription, no account.

loc.title: 年終報告簡報只做一頁：考核、尾牙前怎麼把一整年講清楚
loc.meta: 年終考核報告不用 20 頁。用「三個成果＋一個數字＋明年一件事」把一整年收成一頁，主管三十秒看懂。附結構、取捨方法與常見問題。
loc.h1: 年終報告簡報一頁版：把一整年收成主管三十秒看得懂的一頁
loc.lead: 年底考核、部門回顧、尾牙前的主管會議，大家都在交年終報告。主管一天可能要看十幾份，真正會被記住的，通常只有第一頁上的那幾句話。
loc.answer: 一頁年終報告的骨架是：最上面一句結論（今年最重要的貢獻），中間三個成果，各配一個前後對比的數字，最下面一行寫明年要推的一件事與需要的支援。其他細節放附件，不放進這一頁。
paras: 最難的不是排版，而是取捨。先把今年做過的事全部列出來，再用一個問題篩：「如果這件事沒做，團隊或公司會少什麼？」答得出具體後果的才留下。通常會剩五到八件，再挑最能代表你今年角色的三件。日常維運、支援別人的工作很重要，但除非有可以量化的結果，否則放到附件或口頭補充就好。
每個成果都要有「之前 → 之後」。「優化報表流程」看不出份量，「月報製作從 3 天縮短到半天」就很清楚。數字一定要能對得上原始資料，考核時主管很可能會追問來源；沒有數字的成果，可以寫成具體範圍，例如「接手 4 個客戶、全數續約」。最後一行寫明年要做的一件事，以及你需要什麼資源，這一行常常是考核面談真正會討論的地方。
如果手上的素材是一整年的週報、會議紀錄或試算表，可以交給 OnePage PPT 先排出第一版：打字、貼上、拍照或匯入 PDF 與試算表，點「產生投影片」就會把內容整理成標題重點，數字變成直條圖、折線圖等合適的圖表，日期變成時間軸，而且只有在資料撐得住時才會畫圖、不會自行編造數字。可匯出可編輯的 .pptx、PDF 或高解析 PNG；所有處理都在裝置上完成。

給主管看的主頁一頁就夠，重點是讓對方三十秒內知道你今年的貢獻。細節、過程與佐證資料可以放附件，面談時被問到再打開。

改寫成具體範圍或結果，例如「負責 4 個客戶、全數續約」「支援 3 個部門導入新系統」。比起形容詞，具體的對象與數量更有說服力。

en.title: One-slide year-end review: summarize your whole year on a single page
en.meta: A year-end performance review doesn't need 20 slides. One headline, three results with before-and-after numbers, and one ask for next year fit on one page.
en.h1: One-slide year-end review: a whole year your manager can read in 30 seconds
en.lead: At year-end review time, managers may read a dozen self-reviews in a day. What sticks is usually the few lines on the first page.
en.answer: Structure the slide as one headline sentence (your biggest contribution this year), three results each with a before-and-after number, and one bottom line naming next year's priority and the support you need. Everything else goes in an appendix.
paras: The hard part is cutting, not layout. List everything you did, then filter with one question: "If I hadn't done this, what would the team have lost?" Keep only items with a concrete answer — usually five to eight — and pick the three that best show your role this year. Maintenance and helping others matter, but unless there's a measurable result, mention them verbally or in the appendix.

Every result needs a before and after. "Improved reporting" means little; "monthly report cut from three days to half a day" is clear. Make sure every number traces back to a source, because reviewers ask. Without a number, use concrete scope: "took over 4 accounts, all renewed". The last line — next year's priority and what you need — is often what the review conversation actually turns on.

If your raw material is a year of weekly updates, meeting notes or spreadsheets, OnePage PPT can draft the first version: type, paste, snap a photo or import a PDF or spreadsheet, tap Make My Slide, and the content is summarised into headlines and turned into the right visual — numbers into charts, dates into a timeline — and it only draws a chart when the data supports it. Export an editable .pptx, a PDF or a high-resolution PNG.

Use concrete scope or outcomes, such as "supported 3 teams through a system rollout". Specific counts beat adjectives.

Depois divida o preço da oferta por esse valor. Uma TV que parecia uma pechincha vira “quatro dias de trabalho”, e um fone com 50% de desconto ainda pode custar uma tarde inteira. Ver o número em horas tira o efeito do preço riscado e deixa a comparação honesta.

en.title: Is a Black Friday deal worth it? The work-hours test
en.meta: Before checkout on Black Friday (Nov 27, 2026), turn the price into hours of work and tag it as need, want or impulse. Then you know if it's worth it.
en.h1: Is a Black Friday deal worth it? Count it in hours, not percent off
en.lead: A discount tells you what you save. It does not tell you how much of your week the purchase takes. That second number is what decides it.
en.answer: A deal is worth it when the item was on your list before Black Friday, the price is genuinely lower than in the previous weeks, and the hours of work it costs feel fair for how much you will use it.
paras: Black Friday 2026 is on November 27, but deals start weeks earlier, which creates pressure to decide fast. “Is it worth buying?” really has three parts: did I need this before the sale, is the discount real, and how much of my time does it cost. If the first answer is no, the percentage off does not matter.

For the third part, work out your take-home value per hour: what lands in your account each month divided by the hours you actually give to work, commute included. Then divide the sale price by that figure. A TV that looked like a steal becomes four days of work, and half-price headphones can still cost a full afternoon. Seeing hours instead of a crossed-out price makes the comparison honest.

HoursTag Lite does this conversion on iPhone: enter your income, see your take-home value per work hour, and every price shows up as work time. You can tag each purchase as Need, Want or Impulse and follow your value pattern. Everything stays on the device, with no account and no tracking, for one payment with no subscription.

faq: How do I tell if a Black Friday discount is real?
Note the price of the items you want a few weeks ahead and compare on the day. The store's crossed-out price is not a reliable reference; the price you saw earlier is.
Buy on Black Friday or wait for Christmas?
If it is a need and the price really dropped, buying now makes sense. If it is a want, putting the cost in hours next to it usually settles the question better than the calendar does.

loc.lead: Die meisten Fehlkäufe sehen im Moment des Kaufs vernünftig aus. Sie scheitern an Fragen, die niemand vor dem Klick gestellt hat.
loc.answer: Fehlkäufe vermeidest du, indem du bis Anfang November eine feste Liste mit Referenzpreisen anlegst, am Aktionstag nur diese Liste abarbeitest und jeden Kauf vorher auf Passform, Kompatibilität, Rückgabe und Arbeitszeit prüfst.
paras: Ein Fehlkauf ist selten das teure Gerät, das du lange wolltest. Es sind die Dinge daneben: das zweite Ladegerät, der Mixer, der im Schrank landet, der Pullover in der Größe, die beim Hersteller anders ausfällt. Am Black Friday, dieses Jahr am 27. November und mit Cyber Monday am 30. November, wirken Countdown-Timer und „nur noch 3 verfügbar“ genau auf diese Nebenkäufe. Deshalb beginnt Fehlkauf-Vermeidung vorher, nicht im Warenkorb.

Die zweite Fehlerquelle ist das Produkt selbst. Prüfe vor dem Kauf, ob das Modell wirklich das ist, das du verglichen hast – Aktionsware ist manchmal eine ältere Generation oder eine abgespeckte Variante mit ähnlichem Namen. Kontrolliere Maße, Anschlüsse, Größentabelle und die Rückgabebedingungen des Händlers, gerade bei Marktplatz-Angeboten von Drittverkäufern.

Die letzte Frage ist die ehrlichste: Wie viele Stunden Arbeit kostet das? HoursTag Lite rechnet Preise anhand deines Nettowerts pro Arbeitsstunde in Arbeitszeit um und lässt dich jeden Kauf als Bedarf, Wunsch oder Impuls einordnen. Mit „Was kostet ein Ziel?“ siehst du außerdem, wie viel Arbeit hinter einem größeren Vorhaben steckt, das ein Spontankauf verschieben würde.

en.title: How to avoid Black Friday regret purchases: a pre-checkout checklist
en.meta: Black Friday regret buys (Nov 27, 2026) start before the click: no list, no reference price, no hours check. Use this checklist and keep only what you will use.
en.h1: Avoid Black Friday regret purchases: settle it before checkout, not at the return desk
en.lead: Most regret purchases look sensible at the moment you buy. They fail on questions nobody asked before the click.
en.answer: Avoid regret purchases by building a fixed list with reference prices by early November, shopping only that list on the day, and checking every item for fit, compatibility, returns and work-hour cost before you pay.
paras: A regret purchase is rarely the big item you wanted for months. It is the things next to it: the second charger, the blender that ends up in a cupboard, the sweater in a size that runs differently with that brand. On Black Friday, November 27 this year, with Cyber Monday on November 30, countdown timers and “only 3 left” work on exactly these side purchases. So avoiding them starts before the basket.

The second source of regret is the product itself. Check that the model is really the one you compared — sale stock is sometimes an older generation or a cut-down variant with a similar name. Check dimensions, ports, the size chart and the seller's return conditions, especially for marketplace offers from third-party sellers.

The last question is the most honest one: how many hours of work does it cost? HoursTag Lite converts prices into work time from your take-home value per work hour and lets you tag each purchase as Need, Want or Impulse. With “What will a goal cost?” you also see the work behind a bigger plan that an impulse buy would push back.

Is it exactly the model you compared, not a variant?
Do dimensions, size and ports match what you already own?
What are this seller's return conditions?

steps: By early November, make a list and note today's price for each item as your reference.
Set a cap in work hours for the whole sale period.
On the day, open only items from the list; new ideas go onto a waiting list.
Before paying, check the model number, dimensions, size chart and return conditions.
Look at the waiting list again after 48 hours and only then decide.

faq: How do I spot a fake deal?
Compare with the price you noted yourself weeks earlier. A high crossed-out price says nothing about what the item actually sold for recently.
Black Friday or Cyber Monday — when should I buy?
If an item from your list is below your reference price on Black Friday, buy it then. Waiting for an even better price often ends with buying something on both days.

No. Everything stays on your device with no account and no tracking. You pay once and keep it, with no subscription.

loc.lead: 年末年始に海外へ行くなら、パスポートの残存期間を今のうちに確認しておきましょう。写真は自分で撮れば、思い立った日に申請の準備ができます。
loc.answer: 明るい窓際で無地の壁を背に、スマホを目の高さに置いて正面から撮り、規定のサイズ（日本の旅券では一般に縦45×横35mm）と顔の大きさに合わせてトリミングすれば自分で用意できます。ただし規格は変わることがあるので、申請前に外務省や申請窓口の最新の要件を必ず確認してください。

en.title: Taking your own passport photo before a year-end trip
en.meta: Renewing your passport before a holiday trip? You can take the photo at home and crop it to the exact size. Shooting tips and what to check before you apply.
en.h1: Take your own passport photo: get it done in time for a year-end trip
en.lead: If you are flying over the year-end holidays, check how long your passport has left now. Taking the photo yourself means you can prepare the application the day you decide.
en.answer: Shoot facing a bright window against a plain wall with the phone at eye level, then crop to the required size and head proportion (35×45 mm is common for many passports). Specs differ and change, so always check the issuing authority's current requirements before you apply.
paras: Year-end departures bunch up between late December and early January. Some destinations require a minimum validity left on your passport, and by the time you notice, renewal may not be back in time. Processing takes days and offices get busy before the holidays, so having photos ready and applying in November takes the stress out. Check the processing time with your passport office.

The three usual problems with DIY photos are shadows, tilt and head size. Facing a window in daylight keeps shadows off your face, and a white or pale plain wall works as a background. Hold the phone at eye level a little way back; stepping back and cropping later distorts the face less than zooming in. Check that glasses glare or hair is not covering your eyes or eyebrows.

Snapport Lite handles the finishing. Pick one of 35 presets for 28 countries and regions, such as 35×45 mm or 2×2 in, and on-device face detection shows head-top, eye-line and chin guides so you can pinch, drag and rotate into place. You can switch the background to white and lay several copies out on a 4×6 in, A4 or Letter sheet with cut guides. Photos are processed on the device, and acceptance is not guaranteed, so check the official requirements before submitting.

en.title: Year-end overseas trip checklist: from two weeks out to the airport
en.meta: Holiday trips abroad mean passport validity, entry rules and a destination in another season. A checklist split into two weeks out, three days out and the day.
en.h1: Year-end overseas trip checklist: pack by timing, not by memory
en.lead: With holiday trips, flights get booked early and preparation piles up at the last minute. Splitting the checklist by timing cuts what you forget.
en.answer: Two weeks out, check passport validity and entry requirements; three days out, sort data, payment cards and adapters; the day before, pack clothes and carry-on-only items. That covers a year-end trip without gaps.
paras: The worst mistake on a holiday trip is paperwork, not luggage. Countries set different minimum passport validity, and some require an electronic travel authorization or visa. Issuing offices get busy at year end, so check passport and entry rules two weeks out first and keep flight and hotel confirmations in one place.

Pack for the destination's season. Japan or Europe means a padded jacket, gloves and heat packs; Southeast Asia or Australia means short sleeves and sunscreen, and it helps to decide where your winter coat goes after departure. Power banks cannot go in checked luggage, so keep them in your carry-on, and three days out confirm an adapter for the local voltage and plugs, roaming or an eSIM, and a card that works abroad.

Organizing the plan matters as much as the packing. TripBee Lite is a planner built around one active trip: put flights, hotels and plans on a day-by-day timeline and keep notes, reminders and ticket references with them, so you are not digging through email for a booking number at the airport. A one-time Premium purchase adds the smart packing list.

Check passport and entry rules at least two weeks out. Offices are busy at year end, so you need time if something has to be fixed.

en.title: Travel money apps: how not to overspend on a holiday trip abroad
en.meta: On a holiday trip abroad, local prices blur what you spent. Log in local currency, check it in your home currency, set a daily cap and split cash from card.
en.h1: Managing money on a trip abroad: log in local currency, read it in yours
en.lead: Abroad, both the digits and the currency are different, so it is easy to lose track of what you spent. Sort it during the trip so the card statement back home holds no surprises.
en.answer: The simplest method is an app that lets you log every payment in the local currency and see it converted to your home currency on the spot, plus a daily cap and categories set before you leave. Card charges vary with the rate and fees, so treat the log as a guide.
paras: Holiday trips land in an expensive season for flights and hotels, and spending on the ground also rises with gifts and New Year events. Local price tags do not match your sense of value at home, so small payments add up before you notice you are over budget. Setting a daily cap before departure and logging by category — food, transport, shopping, sightseeing — prevents most overspending.

Expect logged amounts and actual charges to differ. The conversion rate in an app is a reference; your card issuer's rate, fees and exchange-counter rates are different. Log cash and card separately and note the rate when you exchange cash, so the statement is easy to reconcile later. Banks and exchange counters may keep shorter hours over the holidays, so get cash early.

G+Money Lite is a trip spending app: log in the local currency and see it instantly in your home currency. It fetches the latest rates automatically or lets you set them yourself, and works offline with saved rates. An optional daily limit shows how each day tracks against it, and you can review by category and by trip. Data stays on the device, with no account.

loc.meta: An Weihnachten bist du der IT-Support der Familie. So findest du heraus, ob WLAN, Router oder Anschluss schuld sind – und hältst es für den Anbieter fest.
loc.h1: WLAN-Probleme bei den Eltern beheben: erst eingrenzen, dann reparieren

Halte die Ergebnisse fest, damit deine Eltern nach den Feiertagen dem Anbieter konkrete Fakten nennen können.

Jede Ursache hat eine andere Lösung.

Teste systematisch: Direkt neben dem Router und dann in den Räumen, wo es Probleme gibt. Geht es am Router gut und im Wohnzimmer schlecht, liegt es meist an Reichweite, dicken Wänden oder dem Standort des Routers – oft steht er im Flur hinter der Tür oder im Schrank. Geht es auch am Router schlecht, sind Router oder Anschluss die Kandidaten; dann hilft ein Neustart, ein Blick auf die Statusanzeigen und notfalls eine Störungsmeldung. en.title: Fixing your parents' Wi-Fi over Christmas: a holiday checklist
en.meta: At Christmas you're the family IT desk. Find out whether the Wi-Fi, the router or the line is at fault, and write it down so the provider gets real facts.
en.h1: Fix your parents' Wi-Fi: narrow it down first, then repair
en.lead: “The internet is broken” can mean many things. Narrowing down whether Wi-Fi, DNS or the line is the problem means you fix the right thing over Christmas.
en.answer: First test right next to the router to see whether the Wi-Fi itself works, then whether the internet and name resolution (DNS) respond, and then compare the rooms where it struggles. Write the results down so your parents can give the provider concrete facts after the holidays.
paras: Many people spend the holidays at their parents', and by the first family video call it is obvious the living-room Wi-Fi keeps dropping. Before restarting the router or buying a repeater, ask where the problem is: is the phone poorly connected to the Wi-Fi, is the router not getting internet, or is only name resolution failing? Each cause has a different fix.

Test methodically: right by the router, then in the problem rooms. If it is fine at the router and poor in the living room, the cause is usually range, thick walls or where the router sits — often in a hallway behind a door or inside a cabinet. If it is poor at the router too, the router or the line is the suspect; restart it, look at the status lights and, if needed, report a fault. Note the time and place of each test, because evening problems look different from morning ones.

WiFi Aid Lite takes the guesswork out: Run a Check tests Wi-Fi, DNS and internet in one tap, Deep Check collects more evidence and stability samples, and “Connection looks unstable” shows the variation. Evidence covers DNS, TCP, TLS, TTFB, HTTP, Direct IP, IPv4 and IPv6, and Check History stays private on the device — handy for comparing tests from different rooms.

loc.title: 寒假作息表怎麼排？3–7 歲孩子不失控的固定錨點法
loc.meta: 寒假不用排到每半小時。抓住起床、三餐、刷牙、睡覺四個固定錨點，其餘時間留白，開學前一週再把起床時間調回來，孩子比較不會作息大亂。
loc.h1: 寒假孩子作息表：先固定四個錨點
loc.lead: 放寒假第一週最常見的狀況是：晚睡、晚起、早餐變午餐，到了開學前一天全家一起崩潰。問題通常不是表排得不夠細，而是太細。
loc.answer: 幫三到七歲孩子排寒假作息，只要固定起床、三餐、刷牙、睡覺這幾個錨點，錨點之間保留彈性；過年前後允許鬆一點，開學前一週再逐天把起床時間拉回上學時間。
paras: 學齡前與低年級的孩子還看不懂時鐘上的「九點半到十點」，細到每半小時的作息表，最後多半只有大人在執行。比較可行的是用「事件」排順序：起床後先刷牙、吃完早餐才出門、晚餐後洗澡、洗完澡講故事。孩子記得住順序，就不必每件事都由大人催。
寒假剛好跨過農曆新年，回鄉下、走春、守歲都會打亂睡眠。與其硬撐表格，不如先講好「哪幾天是例外」，例外結束隔天就回到原本的錨點。起床時間若一次往前調太多，孩子容易整天鬧脾氣，開學前一週每天提早一點點比較溫和。

en.title: Winter break routine for kids 3–7: the anchor method
en.meta: Skip the half-hour timetable. Fix four anchors (wake-up, meals, teeth, bedtime), leave the rest flexible, and shift wake-up back the week before school.
en.h1: A winter break routine for young kids: four fixed anchors
en.lead: The usual winter break slide: late nights, late mornings, breakfast turning into lunch, and a meltdown the night before school starts. The fix is usually a simpler chart, not a stricter one.
en.answer: For children aged three to seven, fix wake-up, meals, tooth brushing and bedtime, keep everything between them flexible, allow planned exceptions over holidays, and bring wake-up time back gradually during the last week of the break.
paras: Young children cannot follow "9:30 to 10:00". A timetable that detailed ends up being run by the adults alone. Sequencing works better: teeth after waking, shoes on only after breakfast, bath after dinner, story after bath. Once a child knows the order, you stop issuing every instruction yourself.

Holidays will break the rhythm: travel, late family dinners, visitors. Rather than defending the chart every day, name the exception days in advance and return to the anchors the morning after. Moving wake-up time by a lot in one go tends to produce a grumpy day, so small daily steps in the final week are gentler.

Motivation comes from feedback that arrives right away. A cheer the moment teeth are brushed works better than a sticker tallied on Sunday. Lumi Mission Planet turns meals, tooth brushing, sleep and tidy-up into small missions parent and child tap together, with an instant reaction for every step and a seven-day calendar in the parent dashboard.

Between anchors, set an order, not clock times.
Leave one block each day for your child to choose, so the chart is not just a list of orders.

In the final week, move wake-up a little earlier each day until it matches school days.

No. Keep wake-up and bedtime within about an hour of school days and adjust back in the last week.

loc.title: 寒假注音複習：小一孩子不退步的每天十分鐘
loc.meta: 小一上學期剛學完注音，寒假一放就容易忘聲調、拼不出來。每天十分鐘，輪流練聽音、聲調、拼讀和書寫，比開學前一次狂補有效。
loc.h1: 寒假注音複習：別讓小一上學期的注音退回去
loc.lead: 一年級上學期的注音才剛熟，寒假一放三週以上，開學後常見的是：符號認得，拼起來卡住；二聲三聲分不清；ㄓㄗ、ㄣㄥ又混在一起。
loc.answer: 寒假複習注音不必寫整本評量。每天十分鐘，分成聽音辨認、聲調、拼讀、書寫四種輪流練，並把重點放在孩子上學期最常錯的那幾組，開學時通常就能接得上。
paras: 注音退步最先掉的往往不是符號本身，而是「拼」：看到ㄒ、ㄧ、ㄠ三個符號，能一個一個唸，卻合不成「ㄒㄧㄠ」。所以複習時拼讀要佔最多時間，從兩拼開始，再到三拼，聲母固定、韻母換掉，一次練一組。
第二個容易退的是聲調。二聲和三聲最常混淆，可以用手勢幫忙：二聲手往上揚，三聲手先往下再往上。過年期間跟長輩講話、看春聯，都是隨手練聲調的機會，例如請孩子用注音拼出「恭喜」「紅包」再標調。
書寫可以少量但要正確：每天挑三個容易寫錯筆順的符號就好。想讓孩子願意天天回來練，可以用 Lumi 注音星球：餵食小夥伴練聽音選符號、魔法描寫練筆順、聲調雲霄飛車分辨四聲、拼音小火車練聲母介音韻母拼讀，完全無廣告。

en.title: Winter break Zhuyin review for first graders: 10 minutes a day
en.meta: First graders often lose Zhuyin blending and tones over a long break. Ten minutes a day of listening, tones, blending and writing keeps them on track.
en.h1: Keeping first-grade Zhuyin from slipping over winter break
en.lead: Children in Taiwan finish learning Zhuyin in the first semester of first grade. After a few weeks off, the usual problems are blending that stalls, second and third tones mixed up, and similar-sounding symbols confused again.
en.answer: Skip the full workbook. Spend ten minutes a day rotating listening, tones, blending and writing, focused on the symbol groups your child got wrong most often last semester.
paras: What slips first is usually not the symbols but blending: a child can say ㄒ, ㄧ and ㄠ one by one but cannot merge them into one syllable. Give blending the most time. Start with two-part syllables, keep the initial fixed and swap the final, one group at a time.

Tones slip next, especially second versus third. A hand gesture helps: rising hand for second tone, dip then rise for third. Lunar New Year gives free practice; ask your child to spell greetings or relatives' titles in Zhuyin and mark the tones.

Keep writing short but correct, three symbols a day with tricky stroke order. To make daily practice something your child returns to, Lumi Bopomofo has listening practice (Feed the Friends), stroke tracing (Magic Tracing), tones (Tone Coaster) and blending initials, medials and finals (Sound Train), completely ad-free.

loc.h1: 子どもの冬の服装、気温別の目安
loc.lead: 朝の気温を見ても、何を着せればいいか迷うのが冬。厚着させすぎて汗だくになったり、薄着で震えていたり。判断の軸を決めておくと、毎朝の迷いがぐっと減ります。
loc.answer: 歩ける年齢の子は大人より「一枚少なめ」が基本で、気温は15℃・10℃・5℃を境に考えます。風が強い日は体感温度が下がるので一段階あたたかく、走り回る日は脱ぎ着しやすい重ね着にします。
paras: 子どもは大人より体温が高く、よく動くので、大人と同じ枚数を着せると汗をかき、その汗が冷えて体を冷やします。目安は、15℃以上なら長袖＋薄手の上着、10〜15℃はトレーナーにウインドブレーカー、5〜10℃は厚手の上着、5℃を下回ったらダウンや帽子・手袋まで。赤ちゃんや抱っこ中の子は自分で動かないので、大人と同じか一枚多めに考えます。
数字の気温より大事なのが風です。同じ8℃でも、風が強い日は体感がずっと低くなります。上着は前を開け閉めできるものにすると、公園で暑くなったときにすぐ調整できます。保育園や遊具で遊ぶ日は、ひもやフードが引っかかりにくい服、マフラーよりネックウォーマーが安心です。
最後は子ども自身の様子で確かめます。背中に手を入れて汗ばんでいれば一枚減らし、手足が冷たく唇の色が悪ければ一枚足す。ルミのおてんき星は、体感温度・UV・降水確率・風速から出す0〜100のおでかけ指数と、寒い朝はマフラーを巻くなど天気に合わせて着替えるルミで、その日の目安をひと目で伝えます。

en.title: What to dress kids in for winter, by temperature
en.meta: Dress children for temperature, wind and activity. Simple layering guides at 15, 10 and 5°C, plus quick checks to avoid overdressing.
en.h1: Dressing kids for winter by temperature
en.lead: Winter mornings bring the same question: is this too much, or not enough? Kids end up sweaty or shivering. A simple rule of thumb takes most of the guesswork out.
en.answer: Children who walk and run usually need one layer fewer than adults. Use 15, 10 and 5°C as the breakpoints, go one step warmer on windy days, and layer so pieces come off easily during active play.
paras: Active children run warmer than adults. Dress them like an adult and they sweat, and damp clothes then chill them. A rough guide: above 15°C, long sleeves and a light jacket; 10 to 15°C, a sweatshirt and windbreaker; 5 to 10°C, a heavier coat; below 5°C, a puffer plus hat and gloves. Babies and children being carried are not moving, so dress them like an adult or one layer more.

Wind matters more than the number. The same 8°C feels much colder in a strong wind. Coats that zip open make it easy to adjust when a child heats up at the park. For playground days, avoid cords and hoods that can snag, and a neck warmer is safer than a long scarf.

Finally, check the child. A sweaty back means one layer off; cold hands and pale lips mean one layer on. Lumi Weather combines feels-like temperature, UV, chance of rain and wind into one outing score from 0 to 100, and dress-up Lumi wears a scarf on cold mornings so even pre-readers can see the day at a glance.

en.title: Learning a language as a New Year's resolution: make it last

en.h1: A language resolution that survives past February
en.lead: Every New Year someone promises this is the year of Spanish or English. January brings a course and an hour a day. By February the routine is back and the goal slides to next year.
en.answer: Replace the big goal with a small daily one: five words a day, attached to a moment already in your routine. That is more than 1,800 words a year, and a goal that fits a bad day is the only kind that lasts.
paras: "An hour a day" fails because it needs a free hour. One busy week, you skip a day, then two, and guilt makes returning feel pointless. A one-minute goal leaves no excuse.

Attach study to a habit you already have: the morning commute, the lunch queue, the minutes before sleep. Choose words tied to your real reason. Travelling in summer? Start with travel and dining. Job interview? Start with work vocabulary. Words you will use are words you keep.

The rest is not losing the thread. Wordmate Lite is built around that: each session is a five-word trail, the closing screen shows the five words you just learned, the daily goal can be 5 to 20 words, and your current streak and best run stay visible. It works offline with no account.
